So, on the Brazil one. I looked at the numbers last night. Recurring is somewhere around forty percent, which is lower than the two we saw in Mexico, but the retention is better. Peter, do you have the churn figure?

I have six point four percent annual, but that is from their own deck, so take it as directional. The thing I keep coming back to is delivery. If we fold them in, half of that delivery team is talking to our clients directly within a year.

Right, and that is the piece I want to hear from him on. Not whether they can do it. Whether they have done it. And look, if the answer is no, that is fine. It changes the price and it changes the timeline. It does not change whether we do this.
Agreed. One more thing before he joins. We should be clear that we are talking about a minority position first. Anything else and we spend six months on a structure nobody wants.

Thank you, that was clear. Can I ask you something that is not in the numbers? Of the people who would be on our account in the first year, how many have delivered in English before, and I mean delivered, not attended calls.
One more. If we came in with a minority position first, rather than buying the whole thing, would you still be running the company in three years? Because that changes what we are buying.
